evidence: The frozen agent Dockerfile copies only public instructions/assets (lines 14-15) and task.toml sets separate verifier mode (line 28), so pre-submission image separation is sound. But tests/test.sh launches the submitted app as UID 65534 in the verifier container (lines 104-111) and then invokes RewardKit there (lines 203-209). The frozen verifier Dockerfile installs harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 (line 31). In an existing verifier image with that exact installed version, rewardkit/judges.py builds a prompt containing each private criterion's name/description and passes it to ClaudeCodeCLI; rewardkit/agents.py puts the prompt in the command argv as ['claude','-p',prompt,...]. A targeted probe in that image showed a UID 65534 process could read a root-owned process's /proc/<pid>/cmdline: exit 0, visible_marker True. Thus a submitted app can read private criteria while being graded. The provider key was not shown exposed. See per-row-review/evidence/46/isolation-probe.md. The raw index's cited local-proof-summary.json hash was verified, but scripted golden results do not establish a configured judge or portal grade.
counterexample: A broken server can poll /proc/*/cmdline while RewardKit starts Claude, extract the private -p prompt and criterion descriptions, then serve UI and responses tailored to those exact probes so it earns credit without implementing the general playground behavior. A conforming server does not remove this verifier isolation defect.
suggested_fix: In the shared verifier runner, deliver private judge prompts without placing them in process arguments and isolate the untrusted app from verifier process metadata, then confirm with an unprivileged app-process probe and a configured judge run.
